4. The respondent No.1 has appeared in the Rule and filed affidavit-in-opposition denying and controverting the allegations of the petitioner contending, inter alia, in short, that, the fact that 337 rolls of 100% cotton indigo dyed denim fabrics were sent without any Letter of Credit having been opened by Bangladeshi importer and that presumption of good faith as contemplated by the petitioner will not hold good to override the statutory provision of law, customs have lawfully taken action for auction sale of the cargo as the said item having not entered the country lawfully; there being no letter of credit (LC) opened by the purchaser and cleared by the consignee within the period specified in section 82 of the Customs Act, that the exchange of the correspondence between the petitioner and customs and others are based on misconception of actual facts and that can not override the express provision of statutory law, that the claim of the petitioner that section 82 of the Customs Act has no application and section 138 of the said Act is applicable in the matter do not hold good when read with provision of section 82 with the provision of section 138 of the said Act and that section 138 of the said Act has no manner of application to the instant matter, the petitioner is not entitled to take delivery of cargo as claimed by him inasmuch as customs authorities have already taken action under section 82 of the Customs Act 1969 in consonance with law, that the petitioner has no locus standi to invoke the writ jurisdiction in the form of mandamus or any manner whatsoever, etc. and the grounds taken by the petitioner are misconceived and devoid of substance and do not call for any interference from this Hon'ble Court, and, as such, the writ petition is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. Mr Zakir Hossain, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.1, submits on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 3 that 337 rolls of 100% cotton indigo dyed denim fabrics were sent without any LC  having been opened by any Bangladeshi importer and that presumption of good faith as contended by the petitioner is contrary to law and does not hold good to override the express provision of law which requires proper import documents for import of  goods, that customs has lawfully taken action for  auction sale as the cargo has not arrived in Bangladesh lawfully and there being no LC opened by any buyer, and claimed and cleared the goods by  the consignee within the specified term in section 82 of the Customs Act, that the exchange of correspondence between the petitioner and customs  and others were based on misconception of actual  facts and that cannot override the express provisions  of statutory law, that the provision of section 138  has no manner of application in the case, that the petitioner is not entitled to take delivery of the  goods because customs authority has already taken  action rightly under section 82 of the Act in  consonance with law by selling out the consignment in auction and that the petitioner has no locus standi  to invoke writ jurisdiction in the form of Mandamus or in any manner whatsoever as he has no legal right which can be said to have been infringed. 

 21. The assertions of the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 have also struck at the root of the case of the petitioner. The learned Advocate appearing for the  respondent Nos.1 to 3 has clearly and unambiguously submitted with reference to their affidavit-in-opposition that, the cargo in question entered   Chittagong Port without any LC having been opened by any Bangladeshi importer and the  presumption of good faith does not hold good to override a statutory requirement of law of opening LC, the customs has lawfully taken action for auction sale of the cargo as the said items have not Ltd. Dhaka entered into the country lawfully and not claimed and cleared by the consignee within the prescribed period mentioned in section 82 of the Act, that the petitioner has no locus standi to invoke the writ jurisdiction in the form of Mandamus or in any manner whatsoever as the petitioner has no legal right in the cargo which the customs authority has already sold in auction as per section 82 of the said Act, etc.
